issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Gates: the check that stands in the doorway before work is called good. A green result should mean Directive actually looked. A red result should say what to do next.

What a new person hits: The coverage check is satisfied by tests that only search the source for strings. Those tests do not exercise the program.

Why that ruins the product for them: A small generated project looks tested. The check they were sold is decorating the work, not checking it.

How likely: High for a first project where the agent writes the tests, which is the usual way a new person gets tests at all.

## Verdict

The recorded target does not hold. A string-search test file and a typeof-only test file both satisfy `evaluateForwardCoverage` at this SHA. Pairing matches a path. This tree has no substance check that fails those files.

Recorded target, from the Stop 1 write-back 5787635654: a string-search or typeof-only test file does not satisfy forward-coverage, because pairing reads the test body or a substance check already fails those files.

Method reproduced from that write-back, then run. `git show 20eac1de2e510186bdf813efda44e2e641696a6d:packages/core/src/forward-coverage/correspondence.ts` `isTestFile` (lines 86-107) is basename suffixes (`.test.ts`, `.spec.ts`, `.test.tsx`, `.spec.tsx`, policy `.test.js` / `.spec.js`, `*_test.go`, `test_*.py` / `*_test.py`). `expectedTestBasenames` (lines 125-147) is stem plus those suffixes. `git show 20eac1de2e510186bdf813efda44e2e641696a6d:packages/core/src/forward-coverage/evaluate.ts` `listedTestFiles` (lines 290-312) keeps paths for which `isTestFile` is true. The existence decision (lines 388-401) is `expectedTestPaths(rel, policy).some(candidate => existingTests.has(candidate))`. `git grep test-substance 20eac1de2e510186bdf813efda44e2e641696a6d -- packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts` has no match. The verify verbs next to this gate are `verify:forward-coverage` (dispatch.ts line 376) and `verify:test-boundary` (line 377).

Run, staged mode, `evaluateForwardCoverage` loaded from that file. `isTestFile` was called with the path only: `src/app/page.test.ts` true, `src/components/shell.test.ts` true, `src/app/page.tsx` false.

| Fixture | Report | enforce | exit | missing | existence sentence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page.test.ts` readFileSync of `page.tsx`, `toContain("deleteVehicleAction")` | absent | no | 0 | none | all have forward coverage |
| `shell.test.ts` `expect(typeof Shell).toBe("function")` | absent | no | 0 | none | all have forward coverage |
| `page.tsx` with no test file | absent | no | 1 | `src/app/page.tsx` | missing-test sentence |
| same string-search pair, synthetic report, 2 uncovered branches on line 2 | present | no | 0 | none | all have forward coverage, plus ADVISORY |
| same pair and report | present | yes | 1 | none | existence sentence still present |

The header of `evaluate.ts` (lines 5-16) matches the run: missing `coverage-final.json` skips the diff half; default diff posture is warn, exit 0; `--enforce` is what turns uncovered changed branches into exit 1. On that last row `missing` stays empty. The diff half reads the coverage report (`git show 20eac1de2e510186bdf813efda44e2e641696a6d:packages/core/src/forward-coverage/diff-coverage.ts` lines 98-110), not the test source.

Inventory before any new check: existence pairing (path), diff coverage (report, skip when absent, warn unless enforce), `verify:test-boundary` (placement and production references to test roots), `verify:consumer-test-lane` (runs the declared test script). None of them fail a file for being a string search or a typeof assertion.

## blocks-the-design — A warn-first sibling leaves the existence result green

Evidence. The issue's suggested direction asks for one thin fail-closed check, for example `deft verify:test-substance`, and then says warn-first, same as the 90% per-diff threshold. The measured existence result for both placeholder shapes is exit 0 and the sentence "all have forward coverage". `evaluate.ts` lines 428-433 keep that sentence whenever `missing` is empty, and set exit 1 only when enforce is on and the diff half has findings. The warn row above is that 90% posture: uncovered branches, exit 0, existence sentence still true.

Failure mode. Binding the suggestion as written ships a second warning. `evaluateForwardCoverage` still reports the placeholder as forward coverage. The doorway result the issue calls fed stays green. The same paragraph cannot be both the fail-closed existence result and a warn that leaves exit 0.

Disposition. This suggestion cannot bind as the remedy while those two exit stories stand. The existence result for the two measured shapes has to become a failure with one remediation, or the pain statement has to say the existence sentence will stay true.

Road not taken. Put a scoped predicate in the existence half of `evaluateForwardCoverage`, so `missing` is non-empty for the two measured shapes, fail closed, one remediation. A separate warn-first verb is the written alternative, and the run shows it leaves the existence sentence in place.

Steelman. Warn-first matches the #3514 choice to keep a partial or missing coverage report off the iteration-lane failure path, and a loose heuristic will flag golden-file tests and same-package Go tests. What flips this verdict: a predicate that fails the two measured fixtures and still passes a behavioral colocated test, with that failure carried by the existence result. Discovery-only remains available if the pain statement says the existence sentence stays true.

## sharpens-framing — Scope the predicate to the two observed shapes

Evidence. The three bullets are OR'd on the whole file. The typeof example in the issue imports `Shell` (`expect(typeof Shell).toBe("function")`). "Never imports the paired module" does not fire on that file. "Every assertion is typeof or toBeDefined" does, and one further assertion makes that bullet false. "readFileSync / fs.readFile on a path ending in the paired source filename" matches the issue's `page.test.ts`, and it also matches a file that does that once and behavior-tests the module the rest of the time. `expectedTestBasenames` for `.go` is `${stem}_test.go` (correspondence.ts lines 140-141). A same-package Go test has no import of the package under test, so a universal "never imports" bullet flags a file forward-coverage is built to accept. `fs.promises.readFile`, or a path that does not end in the source basename, misses the read bullet. `expect(source.includes("deleteVehicleAction")).toBe(true)` misses the typeof bullet.

Failure mode. Fail-closed on those three bullets flags same-package Go tests and mixed files, and still accepts a string-search file that imports the module, reads it through another API, and uses one non-typeof assertion. The check's text is the evasion list for the agent that already wrote the placeholders. That input is untrusted test source, and a green existence result is what the gate authorizes.

Disposition. The lean can bind with the predicate limited to the observed TS/JS shapes: a paired file whose assertions are only `typeof` / `toBeDefined`, or a paired file that reads the paired source as text. State the miss (one extra assertion, another read API) in the remediation. Leave `.go` / `.py` pairing on the path rules already in `correspondence.ts`.

## footnote — Adjacent reads do not judge assertion shape

`evaluate.ts` line 234 `readFileSync` counts lines of untracked files inside `changedLinesByFile` (head mode). The staged run above does not take that branch. `git show 20eac1de2e510186bdf813efda44e2e641696a6d:packages/core/src/test-boundary/evaluate.ts` lines 358-377 classify test paths and can record `test-under-source-root` for any matching basename under a source root. Lines 380-407 read file text for `scanProductionReferences` (production file mentions a test root). `git show 20eac1de2e510186bdf813efda44e2e641696a6d:packages/core/src/consumer-test-lane/evaluate.ts` reads package metadata and runs the declared test command. A placeholder that passes its runner stays green there. The enforce row in the table is uncovered branches in a coverage report, with `missing` still empty.
